stemMd: In the third paragraph, the author writes "None of this makes diaries the last word." As used here, "the last word" most nearly means

options.label: A
options.textMd: the final and fully reliable authority on how time is spent.

options.label: B
options.textMd: the closing remark in a research report.

options.label: C
options.textMd: the most convenient method for participants.

options.label: D
options.textMd: the newest method to have been developed.

options.label: E
options.textMd: the method that should be used at the end of a study.

explanationMd:
An idiom cannot be worked out from its parts, so use what the paragraph does next. The sentence opens with "None of this", which points back to the advantages of diaries in the previous paragraph, and it is followed by drawbacks: diaries are burdensome, the volunteers tend to have spare time, and one day says little about a varying schedule. The point is that diaries, despite their advantages, are not beyond question. "The last word" is the final, settled authority.

Replace the phrase with each choice and read on. Only the reading "the final and fully reliable authority on how time is spent" makes the drawbacks that follow work as reasons for the claim. The readings about age, convenience, the end of a study or a report's closing remark leave the list of limits with nothing to support.

distractorRationale.d: The passage says nothing about when diaries were introduced. "Last" here refers to finality, not to time.
distractorRationale.e: The phrase concerns the standing of diaries as a source, not the order in which methods are used in a study.
distractorRationale.c: The paragraph goes on to say that diaries are burdensome, so convenience is the opposite of the point.
distractorRationale.b: This takes the phrase literally, as the last thing said. The sentence is about diaries as a method, and what follows in the paragraph lists their limits.

accessibilityText: A meaning-in-context question about the time diaries passage. It asks what "the last word" most nearly means in the third-paragraph sentence "None of this makes diaries the last word." The five choices: the final and fully reliable authority on how time is spent; the closing remark in a research report; the most convenient method for participants; the newest method to have been developed; the method that should be used at the end of a study.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The sentence opens a list of diary limitations (burden, volunteer bias, one day is unrepresentative), so 'the last word' means the final, fully reliable authority. B is the literal-meaning trap. C contradicts 'burdensome'. D and E have no support in the text. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tolce-verbal-run2) reached the same answer: 'None of this makes diaries the last word' comes right before a list of the diaries' limits, so it means diaries are not the final, definitive authority. B is the literal-reading trap (a closing remark). C is contradicted, because diaries are 'burdensome'. D and E have no support in the passage.]

review.notes: Uniqueness check: the drawbacks that follow the sentence fit only the reading in which diaries are not the definitive authority. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
